fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Scattered Vegetation; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Long Driveway; Single Access Point; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm area near the main residence where emergency vehicles can turn around without backing long distances.
• Keep the full width of the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and overgrown vegetation so emergency vehicles can reach both structures.
• Post visible address or unit identifiers on both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can distinguish between buildings on arrival.
• Clear a direct walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without navigating around obstacles.
• Keep gates along the access drive unlocked or secured with a Knox-style lock box so responders are not delayed at a barrier during an emergency.
• Trim any vegetation along the access drive that reduces the usable width or overhead clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Identify and communicate the single access point limitation to your local fire station so they are aware that all response vehicles must enter and exit the same way.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Long Driveway; Vegetation Along Driveway; Structure Cluster; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Mixed Vegetation; Brush Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees nearest to the structures in the cluster to create open gaps between the canopy and rooflines.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately adjacent to any structure in the cluster.
• Clear brush from the identified brush area closest to the structures.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway to keep it passable for vehicles.
• Cut back shrubs and low vegetation growing along the driveway edges to maintain clear passage.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the mixed vegetation areas nearest to the structures.
• Keep the ground beneath scattered trees near the structures clear of fallen branches, leaves, and dry debris.
• Separate shrubs from each other where they grow in clusters near the structures to reduce connected patches of vegetation.
• Maintain the open terrain areas between vegetation groups and the structures by preventing new shrub or brush growth from filling those gaps.
